dedupe_keys.name: asean energy database system aeds and its gis map of power plants and transmission lines

description: The ASEAN Energy Database System is the ASEAN Centre for Energy's one-stop service for official energy statistics, GIS maps, data visualisations, news and policies for the ASEAN member states, first set up in 2001 and relaunched in enhanced form at the 36th ASEAN Ministers on Energy Meeting in Singapore in 2018; it now also links to SIPET, a set of power sector transition tools (project mapping, transition progress and policy tracker). Coverage: the ten ASEAN member states and Timor-Leste, with country pages. The GIS component is an ArcGIS web map (last modified 24 February 2020) with fifteen layers: power plants for Viet Nam (107), Indonesia (557), Thailand (179), Lao PDR (107), Myanmar (81), the Philippines (717) and Cambodia (42), with names, operators or capacity depending on the country; transmission lines for Viet Nam, Lao PDR (427 segments with voltage, status and operator), Myanmar, the Philippines, Cambodia and Indonesia; Indonesian solar sites and Viet Nam wind points. Format and access: ArcGIS web mapping application and embedded feature collections readable through the ArcGIS REST item API, plus statistics pages and Flourish visualisations; free. Licence: no licence on the ArcGIS items or the pages read. Caveats: the GIS layers date from 2020 or earlier, vary in fields by country and have no stated sources; the statistics tables were not read. Simulation uses: regional power plant and grid topology inputs for Southeast Asian power system, interconnection and hazard exposure models. Related records: the Global Power Plant Database (data-global-power-plant-database) covers the same plants worldwide, and gridfinder (model-gridfinder) estimates unmapped distribution lines.
